articles.author: Adhi sankar
articles.description:
A palindrome is a word, number, or sentence that reads the same forward and backward.
For example:
madam → madam


level → level


121 → 121


racecar → racecar



In this blog, we will learn how to check whether a word is a palindrome using Python.
word = input("Enter a word: ")

reverse = word[::-1]

if word == reverse:
    print("It is a palindrome")
else:
    print("It is not a palindrome")

word = input("Enter a word: ")

This asks the user to enter a word.
For example:
Enter a word: madam

reverse = word[::-1]

[::-1] is used to reverse a string.
For example:
madam → madam
hello → olleh

if word == reverse:

The program checks whether the original word and reversed word are the same.
If they are the same, it is a palindrome.
print("It is a palindrome")

If the word is a palindrome, the program prints:
It is a palindrome

Otherwise:
It is not a palindrome

Enter a word: level

It is a palindrome

Another example:
Enter a word: python

It is not a palindrome

Checking a palindrome is a simple and useful Python exercise. It helps beginners understand:
Strings
User input
String slicing
if-else conditions
Comparing values
articles.title: How to Check a Palindrome in Python

Every time I start a new frontend or full-stack project, the same ritual happens.
We install axios or grab native fetch, and within a few weeks, we find ourselves building a massive layer of custom wrappers, interceptors, and helpers around it. Why? Because out-of-the-box HTTP clients handle basic data fetching fine, but they completely ignore real-world app constraints like rapid user actions, state duplication, and client-side payload security.
Later, every project codebase ends up with its own "homegrown" network utility to solve four specific headaches.

articles.description:
The Scenario


An EC2 instance with an attached IAM role has s3:GetObject on a bucket containing sensitive data. An attacker compromises the instance, extracts temporary credentials from the metadata service, and begins bulk-downloading objects. GuardDuty fires Exfiltration:S3/AnomalousBehavior. The development team needs 4 hours to patch. You need to cut off access now.
This post walks through exactly how to do that — commands, policies, validation steps, and the reasoning behind each decision.
First, identify which IAM role is attached to the EC2 instance. You need the instance ID from the GuardDuty finding.
aws ec2 describe-instances \
  --instance-ids i-0abc123def456 \
  --query "Reservations[0].Instances[0].IamInstanceProfile.Arn"

Output:
"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:instance-profile/P…

articles.author: Joshua Hernandez
articles.description:
Most lead intake automations work on the happy path. A form arrives, the workflow sends an email, and the lead appears in a CRM.
The expensive failures happen at the edges:
the same webhook is delivered twice
a required field is missing
a high-risk message is routed automatically
an API accepts the request but drops a field
a downstream system fails after the workflow has already sent a confirmation
A reliable workflow needs more than connected nodes. It needs explicit states, a review boundary, and tests that prove what happens when something goes wrong.
A practical review-gated intake flow has seven stages:
Receive the event
Normalize the fields
Create a deterministic duplicate key
Validate and classify the record
Pause for review when the record is risky or incomplete
Send only after ap…

articles.author: Illeana Vowies
articles.description:
How to Convert Your LinkedIn Profile into an ATS-Friendly Resume


A LinkedIn CV generator can give you a draft, but a LinkedIn profile does not transfer cleanly into a resume. LinkedIn's PDF export can truncate sections, cannot be edited or tailored, and is not built for ATS parsing. 
The golden rule: Import the facts, then rebuild the document for the vacancy. Dedicated tools like PFPMaker can handle the photo, but they cannot handle the writing.
Treat LinkedIn as a source record, not a document template. 
Strongest material: The underlying employment history, dates, education, skills, and contact details.
Weakest material: The presentation—a public-facing headline, a long "About" section, and a layout chosen by LinkedIn. 
A good conversion keeps the evidence and discards the interface.
